### Theory

#### Constructs
- c\_arousal \(Physiological arousal\)\: Bodily activation indexed by heart rate\, respiration and electrodermal response\. Measures\: heart\-rate variability\; self\-reported arousal\. Boundary conditions\: adults\; non\-clinical baseline\; no beta\-blocker medication\.
- c\_perceived\_threat \(Perceived threat\)\: The appraised dangerousness of internal sensations and external context\. Measures\: threat appraisal questionnaire\. Boundary conditions\: adults\; non\-clinical baseline\; waking hours\.
- c\_avoidance \(Avoidance behaviour\)\: Acts that reduce exposure to feared situations or sensations\. Measures\: behavioural avoidance task\; diary counts\. Boundary conditions\: adults\; waking hours\; community sample\.

#### Propositions
- p1\: c\_arousal increases c\_perceived\_threat\. Mechanism\: Interoceptive feedback\: rising arousal is detected and appraised as danger\.
- p2\: c\_perceived\_threat increases c\_avoidance\. Mechanism\: Threat appraisal motivates protective withdrawal\.
- p3\: c\_perceived\_threat causes c\_arousal\. Mechanism\: Catastrophic appraisal triggers sympathetic activation\, closing a positive loop\.
- p4\: c\_arousal increases c\_avoidance\. Mechanism\: Bodily sensations are themselves feared\, so activities that raise arousal are avoided directly\, not only through the appraisal of threat\.

#### Auxiliary assumptions
- aux1 \(core\)\: Self\-report indexes the latent appraisal construct\.

#### Rival accounts
- alt\_cognitive\: Cognitive model of panic \(doi\: 10\.1016\/0005\-7967\(86\)90011\-2\)
- alt\_biological\: Biological model of panic \(doi\: 10\.1176\/ajp\.146\.2\.148\)

#### Scope
- adults
- non\-clinical baseline
- no beta\-blocker medication
- waking hours
- community sample

3. \[directional\] Higher perceived threat is associated with more avoidance\. \(pred3\; derives from\: p2\)
